I have the complete evidence in hand: full baseline text, full candidate text, the single-hunk diff, the task objective/obligations, and the authenticated public-check observation (exit_code 1 with per-case stdout). My analysis:

- **Scope**: The diff changes exactly one line — `_ATX_HEADING_PATTERN` in `MarkdownFile`. Fence pattern, parse loop, `_build_section`, and both `find_*` lookups are unchanged.
- **Repaired cases (observed passing)**: `# C#` → `C#`, `# C# #` → `C#`, `# Title #` → `Title`. The attached-hash-plus-closing-run question resolves as handled: the lookbehind `(?<=\S)` fires when the title ends in a non-space, so the separated run is stripped while the attached hash stays literal.
- **Contract failure (observed failing)**: `# ##` expected `""` (baseline behavior: separated terminal run after an empty title is a closer; empty title preserved) but observed `##`. Mechanism (inference): when the title is empty, the character before the separator is the space after the marker, so the lookbehind fails, the closer alternative cannot fire, and the hashes fall into the `text` group — the same class regresses `# #` and `#  ##`.

This is a known public mismatch, i.e. a contract failure: the candidate does not preserve the baseline empty-title / separated-closer title contract, so the `current-owner` obligation is not met. No further read is needed; submitting the proposal now.

Let me analyze this carefully.

The task: repair the corruption of the literal trailing hash in the heading title of MarkdownFile. In the current source "# C#" becomes the title "C", and searching heading/section by "C#" fails. Within already-recognized ATX lines, a run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab at the end is the closing marker. Adjoined hashes remain as literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run. Preserve the current trimming, separated-closer behavior, empty titles, levels, source line numbers, fence exclusion, hierarchy boundaries, lookup semantics, and exact original content.

Baseline pattern:
```python
_ATX_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)[ \t]*#*[ \t]*$",
)
```

Candidate pattern:
```python
_ATX_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)[ \t]*$",
)
```

Public check results (observed, exit code 1, failed):
- "# C#" → observed title "C#" (expected "C#") pass
- "# C# #" → observed title "C#" (expected "C#") pass
- "# Title #" → observed title "Title" (expected "Title") pass
- "# ##" → observed title "##" (expected "") fail

So the public check has 4 fixed inputs, and one of them fails: "# ##" should become empty title (the run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space is a closing marker — here the text group should be empty, and the trailing "##" is a separated closing run, so the title should be ""). The candidate observed "##".

Let me think about what the candidate regex does for "# ##":

Pattern: `^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)[ \t]*$`

For the line "# ##":
- marker = "#"
- then `[ \t]+` matches the space after #
- Then `(?P<text>.*?)` lazily matches…
- Then `(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)` — the first alternative requires the lookbehind `(?<=\S)`, i.e., the position before the whitespace run must be non-whitespace. The second alternative `[ \t]*` can match empty.
- Then trailing `[ \t]*$`.

For "# ##", after the marker and space, the remaining string is "##". The lazy text tries the smallest match first: text = "", then the group: the position is at the start of "##". First alternative `(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*`: the lookbehind checks the character before the current position, i.e., the space just consumed by `[ \t]+` — that's whitespace, so the lookbehind fails. Second alternative `[ \t]*` matches empty. Then `[ \t]*$` must match "##" — impossible (no hash). So backtrack: text expands. text = "#": position is at the last "#". Lookbehind: the preceding char is "#" (non-whitespace) ✓. Then `[ \t]+` — the next char is "#" not whitespace, fail. Second alternative `[ \t]*` matches empty. `[ \t]*$` on "#" — fail. text = "##": position at end of string. Lookbehind: preceding char "#" ✓. `[ \t]+` requires at least one whitespace, fail. Second alternative empty. `[ \t]*$` matches empty, and $ succeeds. So text = "##".

Therefore the observed title = "##".strip() = "##". This matches the observed output "##".

What would the expected behavior be? For "# ##", the title is… hmm. The line is "# ##". ATX heading: after "#", a space, then the content "##". According to the task: "a run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab at the end is the closing marker." For "# ##", is "##" a closing marker? A closing marker must be separated from the preceding title by a space or tab. If the title is empty, then… the task says "preserve … empty titles …". Hmm, the task says "preserve the current trimming, separated-closer behavior, empty titles." The public check expects "# ##" → "".

Wait — what did the baseline do with "# ##"? Baseline: `^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)[ \t]*#*[ \t]*$`. For "# ##": text is lazy = "", then `[ \t]*` matches "", `#*` matches "##", `[ \t]*$` matches. So text = "", title "". The baseline treats "##" as a closing marker even when there's no preceding title text — the run is separated from the preceding content by a space (the space after #).

So the public expectation "# ##" → "" matches baseline behavior for this input: the title is empty, and the trailing hash run is a closer. The candidate changed this: now "##" is kept as literal title text.

Hmm, but the task says "adjoined hashes remain as literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run." For "# ##", is the "##" adjoined? It's not adjoined to the title text — because the title is empty. Hmm, tricky. Actually wait — in "# ##", the "##" is separated from the preceding content by a space (the required space after the marker). So under "a run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab at the end is the closing marker" — the preceding title is empty… the rule says it's separated from the preceding title. If the title is empty, can the run still be a closer? Baseline behavior says yes (title ""). And the public check (which encodes the authoritative fixed expectation) says "# ##" → "".

The task also says "preserve the current … empty titles." So the candidate's failure on "# ##" is a contract violation: the empty-title case for "# ##" regressed. The observed public check failed with exit code 1 — this is a known public mismatch, "a known public mismatch is a contract violation, not an opinion."

Therefore the candidate is rejected. The disposition is "reject."

Let me also consider the issue of "a separated closing run after an adjoined hash": the task explicitly asks to investigate this. "# C# #" → the expected "C#" passed in observation. Let me verify the candidate handles this: line "# C# #". After the marker + space, the remainder is "C# #". text is lazy… the first alternative requires `(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*`. Try text = "C#": position after "C#", the remainder is " #". Lookbehind: preceding char "#" ✓ non-whitespace. `[ \t]+` matches " ", `#*` matches "#". Then `[ \t]*$` matches. So text = "C#", title "C#". Pass. Good — the adjoined-hash-plus-closing-run case is handled correctly by the candidate.

What about "# C#   " (adjoined hash followed by trailing whitespace)? Remainder "C#   ". text = "C#": lookbehind ✓, `[ \t]+` matches "   ", `#*` matches empty, `[ \t]*$` matches. text = "C#". Good, adjoined hash + trailing whitespace is preserved as literal.

What about "# Title # " (trailing space after the closer)? text = "Title", `[ \t]+` " ", `#*` "#", `[ \t]*` " ". Good.

Now the failing case "# ##": expected "" (empty title, hashes treated as closer), observed "##". This is a real contract violation: the candidate's lookbehind `(?<=\S)` requires a non-whitespace immediately before the whitespace-separated closer, but when the title is empty, the char before the closer is the space after the marker (whitespace), so the closer alternative cannot fire, and the hashes fall into the text group.

Also consider "# " (just a marker + space): baseline: text = "", closer is empty, title "". Candidate: remainder after the marker-space is "". text = "", second alternative empty, trailing empty, $. title "". No problem.

What about "#  ##" (two spaces, then ##)? Candidate: after `[ \t]+` consumes both spaces, remainder "##", same as before → text "##". Baseline: `[ \t]+` consumes one space, text lazy = "", `[ \t]*` consumes the second space, `#*` consumes "##", title "". So a regression here too, in the same class as "# ##".

What about a title ending in a hash followed by whitespace and a closer, e.g., "# a# #"? text = "a#", `[ \t]+` " ", `#*` "#", title "a#". Correct — the adjoined hash is literal, and the separated run is removed. Good.

What about "# a#  " (adjoined hash, two spaces, no closer)? First alternative: text = "a#", lookbehind ✓, `[ \t]+` consumes the spaces, `#*` empty, then `[ \t]*$`. Title "a#". Correct.

Edge: "# a# #" handled. Edge: "# ## #" → hmm. Remainder "## #". Expected: title? The "##" here is… by baseline: text lazy: try text = "", `[ \t]*` empty, `#*` "##", `[ \t]*` — next is " #", `[ \t]*` can only consume " ", then `$` fails on "#". Backtrack: text = "#"… eventually the baseline probably gets text = "##"? Let's see: text = "##", `[ \t]*` " ", `#*` "#", `[ \t]*$`. So baseline title "##". Candidate: text lazy, try text = "": lookbehind fails (preceded by space), second alternative empty, trailing fails on "##". text = "#": lookbehind ✓, `[ \t]+`? next char "#" no. Second empty, trailing fails. text = "##": lookbehind ✓, `[ \t]+` " ", `#*` "#", trailing empty $. Title "##". Same as baseline. Good — the "##" is treated as literal because it's not at the end (a separate closer follows). This is consistent with "adjoined hashes remain as literal title text, including when followed by … a separate closing run."

Wait, actually in "# ## #" the first "##" is not adjoined to a preceding title (the title before it is empty), but since a separate closing run follows, the whole thing is… hmm, expected behavior under the task: "adjoined hashes remain as literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run." Here the "##" is adjoined… to nothing? It's the start of the title. The title is "##" and the trailing " #" is a closer. Both baseline and candidate give "##". Consistent. No problem.

So the core defect: the empty-title case "# ##" (and generally "# <space> <hash run>") regressed from title "" to title "##". The public check observed exactly this and failed.

Are there other possible defects? Let me think about `(?<=\S)` — Python's lookbehind must be fixed-width; `\S` is a single character, no problem. What if a line ends in a non-breaking space? Out of scope.

What about a title where the last character is a hash and then whitespace and no closer, e.g., "# a# "? Covered above — "a#" is preserved. Good.

What if the line is "# #"? Remainder "#". Baseline: text = "", `#*` "#", title "". Candidate: text = "", lookbehind fails, second empty, trailing fails on "#". text = "#", lookbehind ✓, `[ \t]+` fails at end, second empty, trailing $. text = "#", title "#". So the candidate returns "#" where the baseline and probably the expectation return "". The public check doesn't include "# #", but it's the same defect class as "# ##". The check's "including empty headings" expectation supports the general rule: a separated terminal hash run after an empty title is a closer. The candidate mishandles this.

Hmm wait, but is "# #" → "" really the expected behavior under the task? Task: "a run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab at the end is the closing marker." For "# #", the run "#" is separated by a space from the preceding title (empty). Preserve the baseline's separated-closer behavior and empty titles. Baseline: "". The public check includes "# ##" → "" as a fixed expectation, establishing this rule. So, yes.

Now, the task also says "adjoined hashes remain as literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run." — the candidate handles these (observed "# C#" → "C#", "# C# #" → "C#", both passed). So the fix's main objective is achieved, but the empty-title regression is a blocking contract violation, confirmed by the observed public check failure (exit_code 1, actual "##" vs expected "").

Now, obligations: only one obligation:
- current-owner: "Acquire the current complete owner of the Markdown model and preserve the contracts for title, fence, section, and lookup while repairing only the adjoined trailing-hash handling." Path src/devtools/resources/filesystem/models/markdown/file.py, criterion current-whole-resource-v1.

Yes, the diff shows a single hunk. The full candidate text otherwise looks identical.)

But the obligation includes "preserve the … title … contracts" — the title contract is broken in the empty-title case (title "" became "##"). So the obligation is not fully met → blocking.

This also affects "# #" and "#  ##". Since this is an inference (mechanistic explanation, not independently observed), kind = inferred, severity blocking (root cause of the observed failure; also a general contract violation).

Additional consideration: the candidate's regex has a subtle interaction: `(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)` — if a line is "# a  ##  " (title a, then two spaces, then ##, then two spaces): first alternative text="a", `[ \t]+` "  ", `#*` "##", trailing "  ". Title "a". Good.

So text = ""?? Wait a moment. Wait, the remainder after the marker-space is "a  ". text = "", position at "a". Second alternative `[ \t]*` matches empty (the "a" is not whitespace). Trailing `[ \t]*` is also empty. `$` fails at "a". Backtrack: text="a": position at "  ". First alternative: lookbehind "a" ✓, `[ \t]+` "  ", `#*` empty, trailing `$` ✓. text = "a". Title "a". Good — thanks to the lazy quantifier, we can't take the empty-text path unless the entire remainder is whitespace-only. If the remainder is "  " (i.e., line "#   "): text="", second alternative consumes "  "… wait, the remainder after `[ \t]+` (which consumed at least one space) — for line "#  " (marker, two spaces): `[ \t]+` consumes both (greedy) → remainder "". text="", both alternatives empty, $. Title "". Baseline: same, title "". Good, empty title preserved for "#  ".
